name: Brian T. Moynihan

President, Global Wealth and Investment Management

background_rationale: Trained as a lawyer and spent nine years at a Providence law firm before joining client Fleet as deputy general counsel, then moved into running wealth management and consumer banking businesses.

notable.summary: Bank of America agreed to a $16.65 billion settlement with the U.S. Justice Department and other agencies over mortgage-related financial fraud claims from the financial crisis era, then the largest civil settlement with a single entity in U.S. history.
After President Trump publicly accused Bank of America at Davos of refusing conservative customers, the bank responded that it welcomes conservatives and never closes accounts for political reasons.
Named Dean Athanasia and Jim DeMare co-presidents in a leadership reshuffle widely seen as setting up succession, while indicating he plans to stay on through the end of the decade.
At the bank's first investor day in over a decade, Moynihan's team set a 16%-18% return on tangible common equity target and highlighted a $13 billion annual technology budget.

personal_story.hook: The son of a DuPont research chemist in Marietta, Ohio, Moynihan went from corporate lawyer to running Bank of America.
personal_story.summary: Moynihan grew up in Marietta, Ohio, in a large Catholic family where his father worked as a research chemist for DuPont and hand-me-down sweaters passed from brother to brother. His parents stretched to put all the children through college, and as a teenager he worked jobs including a Bonanza steakhouse and maintenance at a Catholic church. He studied history at Brown, where he co-captained the rugby team, then earned a law degree at Notre Dame. At the Providence firm Edwards & Angell he became the youngest-ever partner, and in 1993 a client, Fleet, hired him as deputy general counsel. Through bank mergers he moved from lawyer to business leader, running wealth management, Merrill Lynch and consumer banking before becoming CEO in 2010.
